newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Pemex says to open new natgas plant Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Pemex says to open new natgas plant Thursday.

text.p: Mexico's explosion-damaged Cactus natural gas processing complex will be back at full capacity with the start-up of a new plant on Thursday, a senior official at state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said on Monday.

A blast last July at Mexico's largest natural gas complex in southern Tabasco state destroyed two processing plants, crimping output and requiring higher natural gas imports for months. Lost production and repairs cost Pemex about $200 million, Pemex said after the blast.
"With the reconstruction of Cactus' criogenic plant #1...Pemex will recover processing capacity lost in the explosion," the official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

He said Pemex compensated for the destroyed plant by boosting capacity at other less efficient sites. Mexico's natural gas processing reached its highest level in four years in 1996, with an average 3.324 bln cubic feet per day (cfd).
Key Pemex leaders will meet in Villahermosa, Tabasco state at the start of operations of the new plant, he said.
Only one of the two ruined plants will be replaced, he said, adding that advanced technology at the new plant will compensate for the other plant.
The second plant, criogenic plant #2, is being constructed at a nearby site and should be ready to begin operations later this year, he said.
Cactus' criogenic plant #1 was built by Empresas ICA SA for contracts valued at almost 300 million pesos.
